items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: waited for Flemming because our trombone player got pneumonia there

ctx.x: And he showed him wherein -- but people -- so when we reached Danzig was where the show didn't go any farther. And they closed the show, but Goldberg was forcing the show to close, because that would mean that he would get a better job and have more money, too. But the show would be less. And for his duty of getting these people cheap, he would naturally raise his own salary. Better to put up one man's salary and cut all the other people. Well, the main people wouldn't stand for that, so the show broke right up…

Friedrichsberg, I think, and waited for Flemming because our trombone player got pneumonia there, see? And, but up in Leningrad we had a wonderful time. We bought some sable coats. I bought a sable coat, and two or three other boys bought sables. And I bought a four carat diamond ring, and things like that. The government hadn't seized yet, you know?
